name: Child Study and Development Center
use: Laboratory school (HDFS): child care and early education for ages 6 weeks to 5 years, plus kindergarten; teacher training and research site

facts.text: The CSDC began in January 1929 as a demonstration nursery school for home economics students; the current building on O'Kane Farm was built in 1988.
It serves 122 children aged 6 weeks to 5 years in four full-time and three part-time classrooms, with 20 full-time staff and about 35 UNH students as teaching assistants each semester.
All seven classrooms have observation booths for college students, faculty, parents and researchers.
A full-day kindergarten was added in 1993, and the center has been NAEYC-accredited since 1999.
Its teaching approach has been inspired since the early 1990s by the Reggio Emilia schools of Italy.

verdict: 1988 lab school on O'Kane Farm with observation booths in every classroom; purpose-built and well regarded, but barely documented.
notes: Only one source (CSDC's own page). Architect and renovations not found. Photos: the official site's images center on children, so I didn't download them as references; no licensed photos found. The old row's description '6 weeks–5 yrs + kindergarten' is consistent; its 'CHHS' ownership is correct (HDFS is in CHHS). No independent reviews found.
